<jats:title>ABSTRACT</jats:title>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Objectives</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Homologous recombination repair (HRR) deficiency is associated with improved immunotherapy responses in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) patients. The HRR genes
                    <jats:italic>BRCA1</jats:italic>
                    /
                    <jats:italic>2</jats:italic>
                    are key regulators of DNA repair, yet their impact on the tumor microenvironment (TME) in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remains unclear.
                  </jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Methods</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Using single-cell sequencing and multi-omics data, we characterized
                    <jats:italic>BRCA1/2</jats:italic>
                    mutation-associated transcriptional programs, immune cell composition, and functional alterations in T cells, investigating the molecular and immune architecture of BRCA-mutant LUAD patients.
                  </jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Results</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    <jats:italic>BRCA1</jats:italic>
                    /
                    <jats:italic>2</jats:italic>
                    mutations were associated with increased genomic instability and poor prognosis in LUAD patients, but predicted better clinical outcomes following immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) treatment.
                    <jats:italic>BRCA1</jats:italic>
                    mutations correlated with an upregulated type I IFN/IFN-γ signature and CD8
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    T cell activation.
                    <jats:italic>BRCA2</jats:italic>
                    mutations were associated with alveolar/stress/inflammatory responses and enhanced MHC-II antigen presentation, linked to CD4
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    T cell differentiation. Both alterations coincided with reduced CD28 co-stimulation and CTL activity, hinting of immune evasion. We identified two tissue-resident memory T cell (Trm) subsets as predictors of clinical outcomes and ICB response.
                    <jats:italic>BRCA1</jats:italic>
                    mutations were associated with CD8
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    Trm expansion, whereas
                    <jats:italic>BRCA2</jats:italic>
                    mutations linked to tumor CD4
                    <jats:sup>+</jats:sup>
                    Trm expansion and peripheral T/NK cell cytotoxicity. Furthermore, a cancer-promoting program activated by
                    <jats:italic>BRCA1</jats:italic>
                    mutation was vulnerable to histone deacetylase inhibitors, which inhibited LUAD tumor growth.
                  </jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
                <jats:sec>
                  <jats:title>Conclusions</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    This study provides a preliminary characterization of the BRCA-mutant TME in LUAD patients, revealing distinct transcriptional and immune patterns that highlight differences in
                    <jats:italic>BRCA1/2</jats:italic>
                    -associated molecular architecture and offer a framework for improving therapy efficacy in LUAD.
                  </jats:p>
                </jats:sec>
title: Molecular architecture of the tumor microenvironment caused by BRCA1 and BRCA2 somatic mutations in lung adenocarcinoma
